# Dan's Motorcycle "Twist Grip Throttles"

Source: https://www.dansmc.com/throttles.htm

TWIST GRIP THROTTLES

![151_throttle.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_throttle.jpg>)

![151_twist_grip_throttles.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_twist_grip_throttles.jpg>)

¶ There are many types of motorcycle twist grip throttles, but they all do the same thing. Open and close the engine's carburetor(s). When a throttle cable fails it usually fails at the twist grip end. This is because the end of the cable is being flexed back and forth repeatedly as you use the throttle. Because of this, motorcycle manufacturers use lots of different ways of pulling the end of a throttle cable.

![151_because_motorcycle_manufacturers_use_lots_different_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_because_motorcycle_manufacturers_use_lots_different_2.jpg>)

![151_because_motorcycle_manufacturers_use_lots_different.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_because_motorcycle_manufacturers_use_lots_different.jpg>)

Honda single cable throttle
Notice the twist grip housing
includes electrical switches.

![151_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice_twist_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice_twist_2.jpg>)

![151_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice_twist.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice_twist.jpg>)

Another Honda single cable throttle
Notice the twist grip housing
does not contain
any electrical switches.

![151_another_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice_2.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_another_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice_2.gif>)

![151_another_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_another_honda_single_cable_throttle_notice.gif>)

Exploded view of a
Honda single cable throttle.

![151_exploded_view_honda_single_cable_throttle.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_exploded_view_honda_single_cable_throttle.gif>)

![151_exploded_view_honda_single_cable_throttle.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_exploded_view_honda_single_cable_throttle.gif>)

Another Honda single cable
exploded view.

![151_another_honda_single_cable_exploded_view_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_another_honda_single_cable_exploded_view_2.jpg>)

![151_another_honda_single_cable_exploded_view.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_another_honda_single_cable_exploded_view.jpg>)

Yamaha 80 Twist grip
with switches.

![151_yamaha_80_twist_grip_switches_2.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_yamaha_80_twist_grip_switches_2.gif>)

![151_yamaha_80_twist_grip_switches.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_yamaha_80_twist_grip_switches.gif>)

Yamaha Exploded twist grip
without switches.

Notice on these examples. The cable is curved gently as it inters the twist grip to lessen the bending of the cable. The less bend there is the longer the cable will last. To help this some twist grips eliminate the bend entirely by pulling the cable in a straight line. BMW uses a gear arrangement like a bevel shaft drive.

![151_bmw_uses_gear_arrangement_like_bevel_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_bmw_uses_gear_arrangement_like_bevel_2.jpg>)

![151_bmw_uses_gear_arrangement_like_bevel.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_bmw_uses_gear_arrangement_like_bevel.jpg>)

BMW twist grip.

![151_bmw_twist_grip_2.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_bmw_twist_grip_2.gif>)

![151_bmw_twist_grip.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_bmw_twist_grip.gif>)

Exploded view.

Some twist grips use a grip with a spiral groove cut in it. A small block holds the end of the throttle cable. This block fits into rectangle slot cut in the handle bar. A small knob cast into this block fits into the groove in the twist grip. When the grip is turned, the block slides back and forth in the rectangle slot in the handle bar. This pulls the cable which, in turn, opens the throttle. I have seen this type of throttle on cheap mini-bikes, small Hondas like the old Trail 90 and of all things, older shovel head Harley-Davidsons.

![151_i_have_seen_type_throttle_cheap_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_i_have_seen_type_throttle_cheap_2.jpg>)

![151_i_have_seen_type_throttle_cheap.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_i_have_seen_type_throttle_cheap.jpg>)

Honda CT-90 Twist Grip
with switches.

![151_honda_ct_90_twist_grip_switches_2.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_honda_ct_90_twist_grip_switches_2.gif>)

![151_honda_ct_90_twist_grip_switches.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_honda_ct_90_twist_grip_switches.gif>)

Honda CT-90 Exploded view.

![151_honda_ct_90_exploded_view_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_honda_ct_90_exploded_view_2.jpg>)

![151_honda_ct_90_exploded_view.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_honda_ct_90_exploded_view.jpg>)

Cheap, mini bike, twist grip
with no switches.

![151_cheap_mini_bike_twist_grip_no_2.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_cheap_mini_bike_twist_grip_no_2.gif>)

![151_cheap_mini_bike_twist_grip_no.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_cheap_mini_bike_twist_grip_no.gif>)

Harley-Davidson twist grip.

Now, just to make things interesting, we also have twin cable twist grip throttles. These throttles have one cable to open the throttle(s) and one cable to close the throttle. Now you might ask why? Well, I remember riding my old trail 90 one winter back in 1967. It was quite cold out, maybe 15 degrees Fahrenheit. I was running about 50-55 miles an hour and I shut off the throttle. Only thing was, the bike didn't shut down but kept right on going! The throttle had frozen wide open! I realized what had happened and reached down and shut the key off, killing the engine. Theoretically, a twin cable set up would have prevented this... maybe. Anyway, that's the idea. You can always close the throttle. I always considered twin cable setups a royal pain in the rear. Most twin cable set ups make it a hard to replace a broken cable. I've seen a lot of guys just take the return cable off and run things like a single cable set up. I DO NOT recommend this. It's really not that much hassle making the twin cable set up work so keep it, if possible. The twin cable set up was all the rage in the 1980's but then seemed to fall out of favor. However, there still are a lot of new bikes with them. I must confess I don't like them. I prefer the cables that just pop off

![151_pop_off.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_pop_off.jpg>)

the carbs.

![151_i_prefer_cables_just_pop_off_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_i_prefer_cables_just_pop_off_2.jpg>)

![151_i_prefer_cables_just_pop_off.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_i_prefer_cables_just_pop_off.jpg>)

Twin cable twist grip.

![151_twin_cable_twist_grip_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_twin_cable_twist_grip_2.jpg>)

![151_twin_cable_twist_grip.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_twin_cable_twist_grip.jpg>)

Carburetor end of the
twin cable setup.

All these throttle set ups are sort of the same for replacement or service. Loosen the cable adjuster and run it in so you have lots of throttle play. Unscrew all the screws holding the twist grip on the handle bar and unhook the cable ends. For lube I like light oil or graphite. If there are any gears or it's one of the sliding designs use grease.

While we are talking about twist grips maybe I should cover grip cover replacement. Usually you cut off the old ones and glue on the new ones. Sometimes you can get them off by slipping a very thin screw driver between the grip and the handle bar. Then squirt some penetrating oil in along the screw driver shaft. Pull the screw driver out and work the grip back and forth. That will get them off in one piece perhaps 30% of the time. I don't like to glue them on because sometimes, for whatever reason, you just need to take the grips off. If they are glued on you will probably ruin the grips getting them off. What I do is this. I wrap the handle bar with plain, ordinary masking tape. I wrap it the length of the grip and then try to put the grip on. If it feels loose I add another layer of masking tape. It's a bit hard to get on but you can take it back off without ruining the grip. If you don't like this method then just glue it on.

One last kind of throttle you will run into is not a twist grip throttle at all, but a thumb throttle. These are used on three and four wheel ATV vehicles. You service them just like all the others.

![151_service_them_just_like_all_others_2.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_service_them_just_like_all_others_2.jpg>)

![151_service_them_just_like_all_others.jpg](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_service_them_just_like_all_others.jpg>)

ATV Throttle.

![151_atv_throttle_2.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_atv_throttle_2.gif>)

![151_atv_throttle.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_atv_throttle.gif>)

Exploded ATV Throttle.

![151_exploded_atv_throttle_2.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_exploded_atv_throttle_2.gif>)

![151_exploded_atv_throttle.gif](<07_Frame_Brakes_Wheels_Suspension/151_exploded_atv_throttle.gif>)

Here are some motorcycle specifications. The first part is just a bunch of general specifications. These are the sizes of chains, batterys, tires, spark plugs, and the like, for current model motorcycles (1970-2001). Then, as I get the time, I'm going to add more and more specs on different bikes. # Dan's Motorcycle "Software"

Source: https://www.dansmc.com/mc_software.htm

MOTORCYCLE SOFTWARE

¶ Here are some interesting programs and software to help you work on your bike. I wrote non of these, and all have been presented, for free, on the internet. I'm getting tired of running around updateing links. When one goes bad I'm just going to host or mirror it. If you wrote it and want more credit for it let me know and I'll give it.

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Several neat programs for cutting and fitting tubing, steering geometry, weight distribution, Etc.

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Engine Sprockets Ratio Calculation with Java Script.

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Here is a whole bunch of automotive Java Script programs and other Java Scripts.

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

This little program calculates the size of your engine.
I found it on a web site and then I lost the name of the site.
I've tried, but I can't seem to find it again. So I'm hosting it.

If it's yours, let me know and I'll give you credit.

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Tuned Exhaust Pipe Length Calculator For Single/Twins/Fours.

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Java Script Engine Displacement Calculator

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Engine Parameters Calculator.
This data is used to calculate the compression ratio,

maximum air intake requirements in CFM.

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Enduro Roll Chart

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

Gear Calculator

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

![153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/153_if_wrote_want_more_credit_let.gif>)

# Gearing Calculator

Source: https://www.dansmc.com/mc_software1.htm

Javascript Gearing
Calculator

Primary Gear Front
Sprocket
Rear Sprocket
Rear Wheel Dia

1 Gear MPH
2 Gear MPH
3 Gear MPH
4 Gear MPH
5 Gear MPH
6 Gear MPH

RPM

Default values are for a 1996/7/8 or 1999 XR400R.

The XR400R RPM range
is up to 9,200 RPM before the rev limiter cuts in - need to double check that?

Realistic dyno runs show 8 to 8,300 as being the max working RPM, unless
engine work is carried out to obtain more revs.

Wheel diameter can vary
subject to tyre choice. Measure roll circ and use C=Pi times D to calculate,
where Pi is 22/7

HRC kit Primary Gears are 24/64 or 2.666 to 1
ratio.

To return the script default values use refresh in your browser
plus the control key.

# Dan's Motorcycle "Days of Yore"

Source: https://www.dansmc.com/yore.htm

Days of Yore

![154_days_yore_2.jpg](<08_Specifications_Reference/154_days_yore_2.jpg>)

![154_days_yore.jpg](<08_Specifications_Reference/154_days_yore.jpg>)

¶ Back in the days of Yore

![154_back_days_yore.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/154_back_days_yore.gif>)

, when the earth was young and Dinosaurs ruled, we tried lots of different things to make our motorcycles run better. Those things are now 30 to 60 years old, possibly more. To some of you, that is a lifetime ago. Maybe, even before you were born. To me, it is like yesterday.

On this page I am going to reprint some old ideas whose time has come and passed. Kind of like me. I hope you find this stuff as interesting as I did.

Coil # 1. Electronic Ignitions were but a dream. However, you could do a lot if you had a coil.
Coil # 2.
Coil # 3.
Letters on Coils.
Coil # 4.
Magneto for the old Honda 450 twin-1969.
Pumper Carbs. The poor man's fuel injection.

Gasohol, wait a minute. Are they still trying to push that?
Flywheel Magneto Stuck on Shaft
Make a Flow Bench

Expansion Chambers #1

# Dan's Motorcycle "Motorcycle Theory Books"

Source: https://www.dansmc.com/books.htm

State of the Art Motorcycle Theory Books.
Just remember it is State of the Art in 1903.

The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be;
and that which is done is that which shall be done:
and there is no new thing under the sun.

Ecclesiastes 1:9

¶ Here is a copy of the patent for the First Motorcycle Engine.
Daimler put in for it on the Third of April 1885 READ NOW

¶ This is a great book from England written in 1903.
"Motorcycles & How to Manage Them". READ NOW

¶ Another great book written in 1920 in the United States.
"Motor-Cycle Principles and the Light Car". READ NOW

¶ "The Gas Engine-How to Make and Use it".
Written in 1897 in the United States. READ NOW

¶ "On the Theory of the Gas Engine".
By Permission of the Council.
Excerpt Minutes of Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers.
Vol. lxix. Session 1881-82. Part iii.
Written in 1882 in London. READ NOW

¶ American Army Technical Manual TM 10-515, "The Motorcycle" -1940 READ NOW

¶ American Army Technical Manual TM 10-515, "The Motorcycle" -1942 READ NOW

¶ "The Motorcyclist's Workshop" -1931 READ NOW

¶ "Gas Engine Construction" -1906 READ NOW

¶ 1500 Automobile Repairshop Short-cuts from 1918. Very informative and interesting. READ NOW

¶ "Memories-of-Plumstead" - 1928 READ NOW

¶ Japan's Motorcycle Wars - 1972 READ NOW

¶ Engineering Fundamentals of the Internal Combustion Engine - 1972?? READ NOW

# Dan's Motorcycle "Miscellaneous"

Source: https://www.dansmc.com/miscellaneous/miscellaneous.htm

Miscellaneous

¶ Well, sad to say, I have worked quite a lot on Lawn mowers, Rototillers, Lawn Tractors, Outboards and other non-Motorcycle engines. These small engines are known as Fractional Horsepower Engines. I was up in my shop's attic the other day and ran across several years worth of old receipts from back in the 1990s. Like detective Joe Kenda always says "My, My, My". It seems I've sure fixed a lot of Lawnmowers in years past. Add to that a big pile of outboards too. Not to mention Rototillers, Generators, Lawn Tractors and most anything with a Fractional Horsepower Engine on it. Ah, the things we do to keep from starving.

Anyway, Here are some Specifications, Tips, Flow charts and such on small engines that you may find useful. If you want to print them out, click the pictures, save and print.

# Dan's Motorcycle Course "Audio."

Source: https://www.dansmc.com/Dansmc_Audio/mc_course_audio.htm

Dansmc Motorcycle Repair Course Audio

One problem. It seems eight of my mp3s don't come thru sometimes and you get a runtime error page.

![157_seems_eight_my_mp3s_don_t_2.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/157_seems_eight_my_mp3s_don_t_2.gif>)

![157_seems_eight_my_mp3s_don_t.gif](<08_Specifications_Reference/157_seems_eight_my_mp3s_don_t.gif>)

To top it off the error can change among the different mp3s. Oh well, I think I got it working... maybe! If it doen't work for you, come back and try it in a day or two.

However, you just have to have those eight audio files right now, don't you? So here they are in a zip file.
